title: Core memory unlocked for sure 🔓 #ImmersivePhantom #Phantomoftheopera ...
transcript: So I just had one of the craziest nights of my life at the immersive Phantom opening night party, including some unprecedented access to areas of the theater where you're normally not allowed to take photos or videos. Like, as you can see, you could take photos with the chandelier. They had a professional photographer taking photos with flash that probably looked much better than this one. And then we had access to each of the dressing room sets, which each contained a different activity. First was some temporary tattoos you could choose from a selection of phantom inspired designs. The second was a tarot reading by Madam Zephyr. And if you've been following this page for a while, you know why that is so exciting. She was a part of a bunch of the marketing events leading up to the show, but then kind of disappeared, so it was amazing to see her again. And then the final room was a caricature artist. They also turned the final layer area into a second bar and dance floor, complete with some really awesome dancers and a DJ. They also had another DJ downstairs at the Lake Bar, which is the area they normally leave open after the show, as well as a selection of food, desserts, and, of course, drinks. The guess list was insane. Adam Lambert was there. I got to meet Diane Hollis, the director of the show, and just gosh about how much I love what she Did with this material. And, of course, Lord Andy was there as well. I did have a brief conversation with him, but I was too scared to ask for a photo. We were there until, like, past midnight, and honestly, I could have spent all night there. I really hope that this was some kind of test run for future events, I think it's an experience that a lot of people would love to have and would be willing to pay for. But, yeah, that was one of the best nights of my life, and I honestly still can't believe that I got to experience it.
reasoning: This is a recap of an opening night party/event at the immersive Phantom production, not a review of the show itself. The creator describes party activities (tattoos, tarot, caricatures, DJs, celebrity sightings) rather than offering opinions on the performance.
